env.world: A two-sample semi-supervised discrete causal experiment. A known covariate alphabet \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge2\), binary treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and binary outcome \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) give the complete record space \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\). A law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)\) determines cell masses \(p_x=P(X=x)\), propensities \(e_x=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) on occupied cells, outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\), treatment--covariate cell masses \(s_{ax}=P(X=x,A=a)\), outcome-marked masses \(q_{ax}=s_{ax}\mu_{ax}\), and the target \(\tau(P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\in[-1,1]\). For a known overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the unrestricted class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the laws with \(\epsilon\le e_x\le1-\epsilon\) on every occupied cell; no minimum cell mass is imposed and null cells are permitted. The observation experiment \(\mathcal E_{n,m,d,\epsilon}\) supplies \(n\ge1\) complete labeled records \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) together with \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\) from the same population, the two samples being independent, so that outcome-bearing information has size \(n\) while treatment--covariate information has size \(N=n+m\). Estimators \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\) are the measurable real functions of \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\); the minimax risk is \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\inf_{T\in\mathcal T_{n,m,d}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E[(T-\tau(P))^2]\), compared with the explicit annotation-frontier rate \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+d^2/(N^2\log^2(en))\}\) and attained by the mixed-information hybrid \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\). Asymptotic statements run along arbitrary sequences \((m_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \((d_n)_{n\ge1}\); the two-sided constants \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\in(0,\infty)\) depend only on \(\epsilon\). Lower bounds are indexed by fuzzy hypotheses \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) on \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) whose full random table \(P_{XA}\) has identical distribution, together with the finite illustrative pair \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}},\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) and the finite calculation \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\) at \(d=2\), \(\epsilon=1/4\).
